stimulus.text: That the only representatives of the people of these colonies are persons chosen therein by themselves; and that no taxes ever have been, or can be constitutionally imposed on them, but by their respective legislatures.
stimulus.source_note: Declaration of Rights and Grievances, Stamp Act Congress, New York, October 1765. Public domain.

books.section: A. Colonial Resistance to British Policies in the Aftermath of the French and Indian War
The Sugar Act, the Currency Act, and the Stamp Act

stem: The Declaration's central claim is that...

options.text: Parliament has no authority over the colonies in any matter
options.misconception: The Declaration claims only that Parliament cannot tax the colonies — the delegates still accepted Parliament's regulation of imperial trade.

options.text: Only legislatures chosen by the colonists themselves can tax them
The king alone may impose taxes on the colonies
options.misconception: The Declaration gives the taxing power to the colonial legislatures, not to the king — the king is not named as a taxing authority.

options.text: Colonial assemblies should send delegates to sit in Parliament
options.misconception: The delegates did not ask for seats in Parliament — they claimed the right to tax themselves through their own assemblies.

rationales.B: The sentence gives the whole claim: 'the only representatives of the people of these colonies are persons chosen therein by themselves.' Taxation belongs to the legislatures the colonists elect.
rationales.A: The claim is narrower than that. The Declaration denies Parliament the taxing power only — it leaves trade regulation alone.
rationales.C: The king is not given the taxing power here. The Declaration assigns it to 'their respective legislatures.'
rationales.D: Seats in Parliament were never requested. The delegates wanted to tax themselves at home, not to sit in London.
rationales.general:
1. Find the sentence's subject. 'The only representatives of the people' — the Declaration defines who can speak for the colonists.
2. Read the second half. No taxes can be imposed 'but by their respective legislatures.'
3. Name what is claimed and what is not. The claim is about taxation only, not about Parliament's power to regulate trade.
Remember: a claim is only as wide as its words — read what a document actually says.
